statement: For three pairwise distinct actual boundary-quotient fiber partitions, lifted through the same source universal covering, the full group preserving each partition and its real target orientation is a closed locally compact subgroup in the actual compact-open topology. It is a transitive Lie group of dimension two or three; any pair image different from the full plane makes the action simply transitive and two-dimensional. The closure of the compatible lifted loop group on that covering plane is consequently locally compact. Original covering equations and the global restriction kernel are retained.
depends_on: C42 common compatible lifts; C43 exact real-line quotient products and sections; C45 pair-coordinate domains and finite endpoint homeomorphisms; verified Polish open orbit-map theorem; explicit invariant interior means; Arzela-Ascoli for maps and inverses; Pardon Theorem 1.5 and its introductory reduction; Palais Theorem 2.3.3 with the free-action local trivialization
manuscript_passages: Section 23, folios 140-141, scans 279-281; Part C(b) infinite-operator request; simultaneous actual boundary-quotient constraints in the remaining frontier extension problem
depends_on_doubtful_reading: None. Local compactness is proved by uniform compact bounds and equicontinuity for automorphisms and their inverses, before applying the Lie-action theorems. Point-evaluation determination alone is not used to infer local compactness.
notes: The common group contains all three real target lifts and is genuinely transitive. Sections prove the exact group topology and closedness. In a half-plane or band, an invariant strictly interior mean makes every point stabilizer trivial by recursive subdivision and fixed-interval propagation. With the other pair images full, this mean is constructed from the unique equation r_s squared of a equals b. A further non-plane pair instead identifies the third action by a finite endpoint map; inverse equations or an explicit integer shift produce the mean. When all pair images are full planes, an explicit isotopy makes the multiplication a global ordered loop. Diagonal roots, translation grids, and inverse evaluation bounds yield compact evaluation strips in its automorphism group. Palais applies to the free Cartan right stabilizer action on the still-Polish full group and proves the required local product with the source plane. Pardon was reopened in the primary PDF; Palais Theorem 2.3.3 and the exact free-action local trivialization were reopened in the original author-uploaded text and Kramer-Murat Garcia Theorem 3.7. No global frontier extension, no operator permutation of an arbitrarily selected triple, and no identification of the original global restriction kernel is asserted.
